name: sentineltx-mcp

tools.name: lookup_address
tools.description:
Look up a blockchain address. Returns labels, risk tags, entity info, balance
and up to five top outbound counterparties, as a short fact table. The
counterparties come from an outbound trace run at the standard forensic depth
of five hops, so some may be several hops away rather than direct.
Works for Ethereum and 50+ other EVM chains, Bitcoin, Litecoin, Solana, Tron
and XRP.
Usually answers in under a minute; past 90s it returns a timeout notice, which
is not a finding about the address, plus a session_id whose finished answer
check_investigation collects. It is not the court-grade forensic write-up: for
that, or for deep fund-flow tracing, call start_investigation — with this
lookup's session_id to continue the same case.

address.description: Blockchain address (0x..., T..., bc1..., r..., etc.)

tools.name: validate_address
tools.description: Validate a blockchain address format and detect which chain it belongs to. Use this before any tracing tool to confirm the address parses cleanly.

tools.name: start_investigation
tools.description:
Start a blockchain forensic investigation. Returns a session_id immediately.

Use for: multi-hop fund tracing, cross-chain bridge detection, suspect-to-exchange
flow analysis, AML / STR report generation, victim-fund recovery analysis.

Most investigations finish within 10 minutes; a deep trace or a court-grade
report can run to the server's 30-minute ceiling. After calling this, tell the
user it has started, then call check_investigation(session_id) again and again
until the status is complete, error or cancelled. Each call waits for a change
itself, so no pause is needed between calls. Do not leave a gap of 3 minutes:
past 10 minutes, the server stops relaying a run nothing has polled for 3
minutes, and check_investigation then reports status=error with what it had.

mode.description: 'investigation' (default) for forensic / law-enforcement use; 'compliance' for AML / STR reporting on a deposit address

headless.description: Default true. When true, the trace runs server-side — no SentinelTX dashboard needed. Set false only if a human user is going to open the SentinelTX dashboard in a browser to watch it run.

session_id.description: Continue this existing case, e.g. the session_id lookup_address returned, instead of opening a new one. The investigation reuses what that session already retrieved. An id you do not own opens a new case instead.

tools.name: check_investigation
tools.description:
Check the status of an investigation started by start_investigation.

Long-polls; returns as soon as the status changes. One call can take up to
wait_sec + ~28s before it returns something — the wait_sec budget, a grace
period for the round trip, then a snapshot if the long-poll overran. At the
default wait_sec=45 that is a ~73s ceiling. Budget for that, not for 45s:
the overrun is real and measured, and this client stops waiting rather than
letting a call outlive the deadline of whoever called it.

Returns one of:
- status="queued"      — accepted, agent about to start; call again.
- status="running"     — in progress; call again.
- status="complete"    — full assistant_text is ready.
- status="error"       — stopped before a final report. Any findings it made
  follow, marked INCOMPLETE, with the case URL. Review them before starting a
  new investigation for the same request.
- status="cancelled"   — cancel_investigation was called; it will not resume.
  Any text gathered before the cancel follows, marked INCOMPLETE.
- status="unconfirmed" — no answer reached us (a timeout, a dropped connection
  or a 5xx). Not the investigation's status, which is kept server-side apart
  from these polls. Call again.

Call it back to back until the status is complete, error or cancelled, unless
an answer says to wait first; a run usually takes several calls. The server
stops relaying a run that is past 10 minutes and has had no call for 3
minutes, and every run at 30 minutes: either reads as status=error with what
it had found.

session_id.description: session_id returned from start_investigation, or from a lookup_address that timed out

wait_sec.description: Long-poll budget requested of the server, in seconds. Default 45. Set 0 for an immediate snapshot. The call itself can run ~28s longer than this.

tools.name: cancel_investigation
tools.description:
Cancel a running investigation started by start_investigation.

Use this when the user wants to abort early — wrong address, taking too long, etc.
Only the session owner can cancel.

Read the returned status, not the absence of an error:
- status="cancelled" — it is stopped and will not resume. In-flight tools may
  take a few seconds to unwind, so one further check_investigation can still
  report work in progress; that is the unwind, not a failed cancel.
- any other status    — the investigation had already finished on its own, as
  that status. Nothing was cancelled and its result stands.

tools.name: get_investigation_graph
tools.description:
Export the fund-flow graph (nodes + links) saved for an investigation, frozen
at the moment of this call. A run that stopped short (status error or
cancelled) exports the graph it traced before it stopped. The result's
investigation_status line is the investigation's status when the graph was
frozen: anything but complete means a partial graph, and a note says so.

Returns a share URL that any HTTP client can GET to receive the graph JSON.
The 24h token in the URL is the credential — no login required for that URL.
Each call mints a new link, and an account holds a limited number of live
links: past it the call is refused (429) until older ones expire. Call this
once per graph you need and reuse the URL.

Set include_payload=true to inline the graph JSON in the tool result, up to
65536 characters. A larger graph comes back as status: too_large, with its
node and link counts and size, and no JSON: GET graph_fetch_url for it. If
fetching the graph fails, the link is still returned, with status: fetch_failed
and the reason: GET graph_fetch_url again rather than calling this again.

Graph shape:
- nodes[]: { id (address), address, label, group, depth (0 = origin,
  positive = hops out, negative = inbound side), balance, received, sent,
  chain?, isOrigin?, sentinelLabel?, entity?, ... }
- links[]: { id, source (node id), target (node id), label? (token), sum,
  sumDict? (per token), txCount, txHashes[], firstDate?, lastDate?, isSwap,
  isBridge, chain?, ... }

A node's balance, received and sent are not the address's wallet balance or
what it moved in this graph. Each is a figure the tracer stamped on the first
transaction naming the address, and 0 when no transaction carried one. An
outbound trace stamps at most the receiving side, so the origin reads 0 there
even when it holds funds and sent every link out of it. What moved is on the
links (sum, and sumDict per token); an address's balance is lookup_address's.

include_payload.description: Inline the graph JSON in this tool result, up to 65536 characters. Default false.
